reference: Polymetallic massive sulfide, Potter Mine (Commons title)

description.lithology: Single slabbed interval visible, cropped close-up of one row. Dominantly fine-grained to aphanitic, foliated/banded metamorphic rock - best described as chloritic schist / altered mafic volcanic - colour heterogeneous olive-grey to medium grey and greenish-grey with patchy lighter grey and darker green domains. Fabric is weakly to moderately foliated/banded, defined by discontinuous subvertical dark green-black chloritic laminae and thin pale grey/white stringers subparallel to core axis in photo. Central sharp-bounded dark black band ~10-15 mm wide, diagonal to foliation, cuts across core with sharp planar contacts and a thin pale yellowish margin on its left side. Groundmass is very fine-grained, granular to lepidoblastic, no visible phenocrysts at this resolution.
description.alteration: Chloritic moderate to strong, pervasive green colour throughout matrix and concentrated in dark bands and lenses. Weak to moderate oxidized along basal edge of core with orange-brown rust staining and along top beneath label where present. Possible weak silicification/carbonatization in light grey patches but not definitive at this resolution. None of the other alteration types can be confirmed as distinct.
description.mineralization: No definitively identifiable massive sulfides at this resolution. Possible trace to 2-3% fine disseminated brassy to silvery metallic speckles scattered through grey-green matrix and as thin discontinuous pale yellow stringers/veinlets along the margin of the central black band, suggestive of fine pyrite +/- pyrrhotite/chalcopyrite, but definitive identification is limited by image resolution, glare and oxidation; otherwise none visible as unequivocal sulfides.

anomalies.explanation: Possible trace to low percent fine disseminated brassy/silvery sulfides throughout the grey-green matrix and concentrated as thin pale yellow veinlets along the left margin of the central black diagonal band, identification uncertain due to resolution and surface oxidation.
Prominent sharp-bounded diagonal black band ~1-1.5 cm wide crossing the core requires geological check to determine if it is massive sulfide, magnetite, chlorite vein, or shear/fault infill.

Foliation/banding is subvertical in the image, subparallel to core axis and to the central band, indicating steep fabric relative to drilling direction that should be verified for structural orientation.
Basal edge shows pervasive orange-brown oxidation/rust and top is partially obscured by white sample label tape with blue text, both obscuring true lithology and contacts.
